answer: Sybil resistance works when identity is costly to fake. In a bonded-reputation scheme, each new agent locks collateral in a vault and earns standing only from staggered peer attestations of work. A forger can spin up a thousand aliases, but each must post capital and build verifiable history; a hollow identity leaves no relic of labor to audit. Sybils vouching only for each other form a closed clique whose signatures carry little weight, so the pigment of their credibility never spreads. The attacker pays twice: capital frozen in the vault, and months of real work before one vote counts.
